questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Explore the nature

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A beautiful nature and being able to understand the local language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Most information is given directly via e-mail or can easily be found through the university's webpage.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were several introduction / welcome meetings.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy. UiB offers housing guarantee for Erasmus students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: When you apply for housing through Sammen, they ask you to give 3 priorities. Do not waste your time on researching the different options – most likely you will be assigned to Fantoft to live in a shared flat.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Housing is really cheap and social BUT if you would rather live alone (and not have a roommate), you should probably find something on your own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Deadline was Feb 1, giving plenty of time to research different courses. Just be aware of altering deadlines depending on the type of course (open/restricted) and the different starting dates. Otherwise, it was super easy and just happened through an online portal.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Nice overview of the different available courses online, being able to ask the faculty, introductory meetings, etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100%. But I only chose open courses, so it might be different for the restricted ones.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time to go through all the different courses from home, so you won't have to stress about deadline once you arrive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found it easier compared to UCPH, but it also freed a lot of time to do other things than study.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A bit more high-school like and less like university. For example, participation in classes was mandatory and there were more assignments throughout the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: "Digital genres", "Old norse mythology", "Schnitzel in a Pita with Hummus: The Anthropology of Israeli/Palestinian Food"

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely the one about food and anthropology. Super interesting texts and a very enthusiastic professor.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Medicine for scabies (fun times). Otherwise none.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Almost everything were less expensive than expected due to a very low currency.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many. Volunteering at bars/music venues, sport clubs, crafting, outdoor activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I chose not to be a part of any clubs; I would rather have the flexibility and free time to hang out with friends and go on hikes and trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hikes. Cabin trips. Consider becoming a member of DNT and use their cabins (ultra cheap if you're under 25).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy since it's quite similar to Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs. Or find a shared flat with Norwegians instead of living at Fantoft.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Norwegians are a bit more reserved.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: All the outdoorsy stuff.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) If you like hiking, this is the perfect place. If not, then expect that 90% of the other exchange students will.
2) Beer is cheapest at Kvarteret or Hector's. 
3) Don't pack for six months, pack for three weeks. You need less than you think.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will find out as you go, no worries.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Hiking. No doubt.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Befriending Norwegians and actually learning the language.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Nope.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
